messages:
jamie: Heads-up — saw a burst of Pending GPU pods in eu-west-1 this morning, autoscaler didn't add nodes for ~3m. Packet shows node groups had spare capacity but CA picked nothing. Anyone seen similar?
sara: saw alerts too. Any `kubectl describe pod` output?
jamie: pasted immediate describe for one pod: `0/0 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.` Also logs show CA considered groups but decided 'would create 0 nodes' in log.
vik: probably expander / priority mapping issue. We moved to `most-pods` for CPU workloads; that tends to ignore GPU-only nodegroups when mixed.
marta: can you share the CA flags and discovery config? we recently added new burst pool (gpu-burst-eu) with different labels.
jamie: current args from deployment: 
```
--cloud-provider=aws \
--node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled,k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/redwood-eu \
--expander=most-pods \
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m \
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m \
--max-node-provision-time=15m
```
(since March deploy)
sara: ok that explains it — `most-pods` biases towards cpu-optimized pools that can host many small pods, ignores specialty GPU pools. Switch to `priority` expander and give explicit priorities for nodegroups (gpu-burst should be high priority for GPU scheduling).
vik: +1. Also bump `--max-node-provision-time` to account for AMI boot + drivers in eu-west: set to 25m. GPUs + init scripts can take longer.
marta: also consider `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` for heterogeneous pools? that can keep CA from trying to evenly spread and instead pick the high-priority group. But test in staging first.
jamie: good call. Any scale-down tweaks for GPU nodes? we saw nodes get removed while pods with local caches were rebuilding.
sara: add `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage` (already default true?), but main fix is ensuring pods have `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false` for long-running stateful GPU workloads or use PDBs. CA respects `safe-to-evict`. Also increase `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 20m for gpu pools so we don't churn after short spikes.
vik: we also use a small annotation-based protection: when a pod uses a persisted model cache we add `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/do-not-remove=true` to the node via a small controller. CA ignores nodes with the `do-not-delete` label — but careful: only use as last resort.
marta: GPU device plugin state can make pods 'unready' briefly; bump `--scale-down-unready-time` to 10m and `--max-empty-bulk-delete=2` to avoid mass deletions.
jamie: trying change plan: switch expander -> `priority`, add nodegroup priorities, increase provision time to 25m, increase scale-down-unneeded to 20m, scale-down-unready to 10m. I'll push to canary.
ops-bot: deploy triggered for `cluster-autoscaler` in eu-west-1 canary (rollout id: ca-roll-2109876543).
vik: after canary, run a synthetic spike test: create 6 gpu pods with different nodeSelectors and watch node selection.
sara: also add logging: `--v=4` for canary to capture CA decision logs, grep for 'considered candidate' lines.
jamie: noted. I'll patch and post results in this thread. Thanks all :thumbsup:
